title: arrangement.edit
description: Edits clips (placements) on the timeline as OpenTune's arrangement view does. The ops are applied in the order given to the arrangement that expectedArrangementRevision names (else REVISION_CONFLICT(arrangement_changed)); each op addresses clips that exist when the call starts, and one call is one undo step. op move moves a clip in time, to another track, or both; op trim moves the start or the end edge of a clip, within the audio of its content (else INVALID_ARGUMENT(trim_out_of_range)); op setGain sets the clip gain, limited to the range OpenTune accepts (warning CLAMPED, data {field, requested, applied}); op setFade sets fade lengths, limited to the clip's length (warning CLAMPED); op split cuts a clip in two at the nearest analysis frame (warning SPLIT_SNAPPED, data {requestedTimelineSec, appliedTimelineSec}, when that differs from atTimelineSec), which needs the clip's pitch analysis (NOT_READY(f0_not_ready) while it runs) and a position strictly inside the clip (else INVALID_ARGUMENT(split_out_of_range)); op merge joins two clips that OpenTune can merge: on one track, the trailing clip starting where the leading clip ends, both showing adjacent parts of one content with equal gain (else INVALID_ARGUMENT(merge_not_possible)); op delete removes clips; OpenTune cannot undo that and no request restores the clips, so a call with op delete needs confirm true, and without it fails with INVALID_ARGUMENT(confirm_required) and changes nothing (PROTOCOL.md section 20.2 rule 3); clients set confirm only when the end user explicitly agreed to delete these clips, and only a call with op delete accepts confirm. A placement that does not exist, or a toTrackId that names no track slot, gives NOT_FOUND(unknown_handle). A clip moved onto a hidden track shows that track (sideEffects.tracksRevealed {trackIds, revert: null}, warning TRACK_AUTO_REVEALED), and a clip that now overlaps another clip on its track carries the warning OVERLAPS_CLIP. changes lists every changed clip with the members that changed; created, removed and idMap (relation split or merge) report the clips that split and merge replace. A trim records the clip's fades in its undo step before the trim, so undoing it restores fades that the trim shortened (PROTOCOL.md section 15.4 rule 2); the result then carries the warning FADES_RECLAMPED (subject the clip, data {fadeInSec, fadeOutSec}, each {before, after}, or null for a fade that kept its length). Split, merge and delete meet a known OpenTune defect (section 15.4 rule 1): the server pushes the same undo entry as the UI, reports undo {undoable: false, reason: upstream_undo_defect} with the warning UPSTREAM_UNDO_DEFECT, and edit.undo and edit.redo refuse that entry. A call with an op split, merge or delete has no other op. The revert recipe of a split merges the two clips with arrangement.edit, and that of a merge splits the clip again at the former boundary; the restored clips get new placementIds, and fades the clips had at the boundary are not restored. A deleted clip cannot be restored: revert is null and the result carries the warning IRREVERSIBLE. With dryRun true nothing changes, and the result predicts the changes (section 14.2); a prediction needs no confirm.

confirm.description: The end user explicitly agreed to delete the clips of op delete. Without true, a call with op delete fails with INVALID_ARGUMENT(confirm_required), unless dryRun is true. Only a call with op delete accepts it.

opMove.description: Moves a clip to startTimelineSec, to track toTrackId, or both.

opTrim.description: Moves the start or the end edge of a clip to toTimelineSec. Moving the start edge also moves the start of the part of the content the clip shows.

opSetGain.description: Sets the clip gain, in dB or as a linear factor.

opSetFade.description: Sets the length of the fade-in, of the fade-out, or of both.

opSplit.description: Cuts a clip into two clips at atTimelineSec.
